Cold that won't go away?

Most colds settle within 7–10 days. If a blocked nose, facial pressure or thick nasal discharge lasts longer, or improves and then gets worse again, it may be sinusitis. Saline nasal rinses can help. See a doctor if symptoms persist, or urgently if there is swelling around the eye, change in vision or severe headache.

Room spinning when you turn in bed?

Brief spinning when lying down, getting up or turning over is often caused by BPPV, a common inner-ear condition that can be treated. Important: sudden dizziness with weakness, numbness, slurred speech, a drooping face or severe headache is an emergency. Go to the nearest hospital immediately.

Dust allergy while cleaning for Christmas?

Sneezing, a runny nose and itchy eyes during house cleaning are often due to dust-mite allergy. Wear a mask, damp-dust instead of dry sweeping, and wash bedding in hot water. If symptoms keep coming back, an ENT check can help plan treatment.

Should I clean my ears with buds?

Ears clean themselves. Ear buds can push wax deeper and scratch the ear canal. Please avoid oil, hairpins and buds in the ear. If your ear feels blocked, painful or has discharge, get it examined.

Is your child breathing through the mouth?

Constant mouth breathing, snoring or a blocked nose in children can be due to enlarged adenoids or nasal allergy. An ENT examination helps decide whether watchful waiting, medicines or other treatment is right for your child.

Teachers: protect your voice during exam season

Hoarseness after long classes is common. Sip water, use a microphone where possible, avoid shouting and rest your voice between sessions. Hoarseness lasting more than 4 weeks should be examined by an ENT doctor.

Noticing the TV getting louder?

Asking people to repeat themselves or turning up the TV can be early signs of hearing loss. A hearing assessment identifies the type of hearing loss and the next steps. Untreated hearing loss can affect work, relationships and wellbeing.

Snoring loudly every night?

Loud snoring with pauses in breathing, gasping at night or daytime sleepiness may point to obstructive sleep apnoea, which is linked with high blood pressure. An ENT check of the nose and throat is a good first step.

Travelling for Christmas? Ear pain on flights

To reduce ear pain during landing, swallow, yawn or chew. Babies can feed during descent. If you have a heavy cold or a recent ear problem, ask your doctor before flying.

Sudden hearing loss in one ear is urgent

If hearing in one ear drops suddenly, over hours to a few days, see an ENT doctor as soon as possible, ideally the same or next day. Early assessment and treatment matter.

Ear pain in children: what to do

Ear pain with fever is common after a cold. Give pain relief as advised by your doctor and avoid putting oil or drops in the ear without an examination. See a doctor if there is ear discharge, high fever, swelling behind the ear or pain lasting beyond 2 days.

Nosebleed first aid

Sit up, lean forward, pinch the soft part of the nose for 10–15 minutes and breathe through the mouth. Do not tilt the head back. Seek urgent care if bleeding does not stop in 20 minutes, is very heavy, or follows a head injury.

What happens at an ENT consultation?

We take a detailed history and examine the ear, nose and throat, using an endoscope or microscope when needed. You will get an explanation of the likely cause and a plan. Please bring previous prescriptions, test reports and a list of your current medicines.

Are vertigo tablets enough?

Anti-vertigo tablets can ease symptoms for a short time, but long-term use can slow the brain's natural recovery. Finding the cause, such as BPPV, vestibular migraine or another condition, guides the right treatment.

Deviated septum: does everyone need surgery?

Many people have a slightly bent nasal septum without any problems. Treatment is considered when it causes ongoing blockage that medicines do not relieve. Septoplasty is done inside the nose and usually does not change its outer shape.

Earphones and young ears

Keep the volume below about 60% and take regular listening breaks, as WHO safe-listening advice recommends. Ringing in the ears or muffled hearing after loud music is a warning sign. Please don't ignore it.

Coin, bead or battery in a child's nose or ear?

Please do not try to remove deep objects at home. Pushing can make things worse. Button batteries and magnets are emergencies. Take your child to a doctor immediately.

Child snoring isn't always 'cute'

Regular snoring in children, especially with pauses in breathing, restless sleep, bedwetting or daytime irritability, can be due to enlarged tonsils and adenoids. Discuss it with an ENT doctor.

Dizziness in older adults: preventing falls

Dizziness raises the risk of falls. Keep a night light on, remove loose rugs, get up slowly from bed, and have dizziness evaluated. Balance exercises (vestibular rehabilitation) help many people.

Sore throat: virus or something more?

Most sore throats are viral and improve within a week. See a doctor urgently for difficulty swallowing saliva, a muffled voice, difficulty opening the mouth, breathing problems or high fever.

Ringing in the ears (tinnitus)

Tinnitus is common and is often linked to hearing changes, noise exposure or ear wax. A check-up rules out treatable causes. Ringing in one ear only, or with sudden hearing loss, should be examined promptly.

When is sinus surgery (FESS) considered?

Endoscopic sinus surgery is considered for chronic sinusitis or nasal polyps that persist despite appropriate medical treatment. It is performed through the nostrils using a camera. Not everyone with sinusitis needs surgery.

Newborn hearing screening

A baby's hearing can be screened in the first weeks of life. Early detection supports speech and language development. If your baby was not screened, or you are worried about hearing at any age, ask for a hearing test.

Can allergy cause blocked ears?

Nasal allergy and colds can affect the Eustachian tube, which connects the nose and ear, causing a blocked or popping ear. Treating the nose often helps the ear.
